title: GPU memory lifecycle budgeter for continuous batching & KV management
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a GPU memory lifecycle budgeter that dynamically allocates and reclaims memory budgets across weights, KV cache, and activations to support continuous batching with predictable latency and better unit-cost. The budgeter should provide per-tenant soft quotas, a multi-tier KV cache (hot/warm/cold), and an ephemeral microburst cushion that can be reclaimed quickly. The system must produce telemetry that enables SLO-aware decisions (latency, tail P99, and evictions) and integrate with the existing runtime routing and fallback policies.

Key features: 
- Continuous budgeting loop: periodically recompute weight/KV/activation budgets from observed usage + forecasted microburst demand. Default cadence 1s with adaptive backoff under stable workload.
- KV tiers: hot KV pinned in GPU memory, warm KV in compressed format (half-precision or compressed blocks), cold KV in CPU memory with async prefetching. Each tenant receives a configurable hot/warm/cold ratio.
- Eviction / prefetch policy: cost-aware eviction that prefers compression + demotion over complete eviction, prioritizes prefetched blocks by access frequency, and uses recency-frequency heuristics tuned for chat vs. non-chat traffic.
- Microburst cushion: ephemeral, preemptible buffer (compressible) sized as a percentile of recent peak token burst (default p95). Buffer is reclaimed in <50ms when higher-priority weight/activation demands arise.
- Latency SLO integration: budget decisions include an SLO penalty term; if predicted impact to P99 > threshold, budgeter shifts to conservative mode and signals upper-layer router to reduce batch sizes or route to lower-latency variant.
- Simulation harness: offline simulator that replays historical traces and synthetic microbursts to validate budget policies before rollout.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Aggressive compression increases compute overhead and may raise token latency for cold->hot promotions. We'll bound CPU/GPU compression ops and measure end-to-end P99.
- Larger hot KV improves latency but reduces activation/weight headroom; use per-tenant profiles to tune ratios.
- Prefetching from cold (CPU) improves cache hit rates but risks wasteful prefetch for low-similarity requests; prefetch windows will be adaptive and predictive (LRU+prefetch scoring).

Telemetry and signals (new metrics): 
- runtime.gpu.memory.weights_bytes, runtime.gpu.memory.kv_hot_bytes, runtime.gpu.memory.kv_warm_bytes, runtime.gpu.memory.kv_cold_bytes, runtime.gpu.memory.activations_bytes
- runtime.kv.evictions.count, runtime.kv.demotions.count, runtime.kv.prefetch.count, runtime.kv.compress_ops.count
- runtime.budgeter.mode (conservative|balanced|aggressive), runtime.budgeter.estimated_headroom_pct
- runtime.batch.window_ms, runtime.latency.p99_ms, runtime.latency.p50_ms

Deliverables: 
- Budgeter runtime component with config knobs and per-tenant profiles (C++/Rust in runtime).
- Simulation harness (python) and a replay dataset for validation.
- Telemetry dashboard (Console) and alerting rules (eviction rate spike, headroom < 5%).
- Rollout plan and playbook for canary/fallback.

Rollout gating: must show simulator pass for three canonical workloads (chat small-turns, long-context summarization, high-concurrency embeddings) and no >5% regression in end-to-end P99 on staging.
acceptance_criteria: Budgeter prototype deployed to staging cluster and exercised with offline traces
Simulator shows <2% false-eviction rate vs baseline for three canonical workloads
Telemetry dashboard created and surface for runtime.budgeter.* metrics
Canary rollout plan documented and validated (5% -> 20% -> 60% steps) with automatic rollback on P99 regressions
Integration tests for KV demotion/promotion paths and microburst reclamation (<50ms reclaim)
comments: 2026-02-02 - Asha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes attached in Confluence. Decided to model hot/warm/cold tiers explicitly and keep kernel for compressed warm blocks on GPU to avoid CPU roundtrips for common patterns. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SERV/GPU+Memory+Lifecycle

2026-02-12 - Miguel Hernandez: Benchmarked compression on A100 and H100; warm-tier compression (fp16 + block LZ) adds ~0.7ms median overhead per promotion but reduces GPU memory by 40-55% for KV blocks. Will add a config flag to cap compression CPU usage per node.

2026-02-25 - Priya Rao (PM): Set customer impact to 'high' for enterprise customers using long-context chat. Requested default conservative policy for enterprise tenants. Adding tenant profile API to allow overrides.

2026-03-03 - QA: Simulation harness integrated; initial run shows reduced evictions on mixed workloads but increases cold-prefetch ops for low-similarity traces. We will add a scoring threshold to avoid aggressive prefetch for low-similarity request streams.

2026-03-10 - Miguel Hernandez: Implemented adaptive microburst cushion calculation (p95 over sliding 10m window). Local microbench shows reclaim complete in ~30ms for moderate load. Pushed branch: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1452
